generalfeedback.text:
Worked out solution

Step 1: The first step here is to pick \(u\) and \(dv\) such that \( \displaystyle \int udv = u \cdot v - \int vdu\).


Step 2: For this problem well use the following choices for \(u\) and \(dv\)

\(u = {@func_var_dv@}\), \(dv ={@func_var_u@} dx\),
Next, we need to compute \(du\) (by differentiating \(u\)) and \(v\) (by integrating \(dv\)).

\(du = {@diff_u@}\), \(v= {@int_v@}\)

Step 3: Plugging the above back into the Integration by Parts formula \( \displaystyle \int udv = u \cdot v - \int vdu\):

\( \displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx = ({@int_v@})\times({@func_var_dv@}) - \displaystyle \int ({@int_v@})({@diff_u@}) dx\)


Step 4: We’ll now need to do integration by parts again for this \(\displaystyle \int ({@int_v@})({@diff_u@}) dx\), and to do this we’ll use the following choices for \(u\) and \(dv\)

\(u={@diff_u@}\) and \(dv={@int_v@}dx\)


\(du={@diff(diff_u)@}\) and \(v={@int(int_v,x)@} \)


Now

\(\displaystyle \int ({@int_v@})({@diff_u@}) dx =({@diff_u@})({@int(int_v,x)@})-\displaystyle \int({@int(int_v,x)@})\times {@diff(diff_u)/del(x)@}dx\)


\(\displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx =({@int_v@})({@func_var_dv@})+({@diff_u@})({@int(int_v,x)@})-\displaystyle \int {@int(int_v,x)@} \times{@diff(diff_u)@}\)

Step 5: Rearranging and simplifying the above function we have the final answer,
